summary: This Layer 2B chunk maps three nuclear-adjacent tickers against Serenity chokepoint logic. BWXT is the strongest relationship candidate in the chunk because it sits closer to regulated nuclear components, fuel services, naval/government nuclear systems, and possible SMR supply-chain enablement; however, the provided evidence does not yet prove that incremental AI/data-center power demand or domestic fuel-cycle reconstruction is flowing into BWXT revenue. UUUU is kept as a speculative shadow candidate because its uranium and critical-minerals exposure may benefit from nuclear-security narratives, but Layer 2A evidence suggests the more constrained chokepoints are conversion, enrichment, HALEU, licensing, and fabrication rather than mining alone. SMR is retained as a high-attention demand-side comparator: useful for tracking whether SMR announcements convert into funded projects, but less likely to be the underfollowed bottleneck expression unless licensing, financing, fuel availability, and customer commitments become primary-source verified.
